title: Tough's mentality, reading and humor
summary: Freeman describes Tough as an educated, music-reading drummer with brilliant humor, and corrects his arithmetic on how long Tough played.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: That is how long it was, 50 years.

Yes, he had been playing that -- Dave Tough, as I say, played professionally at the age of 14 and when you think of this great mentality he had, you can say a man could be an illiterate man and still be a great drummer, but I like to think that Dave Tough's great mentality made him the great drummer, because he was so interested in the -- he was a sensitive artist, he knew about improvising, he knew about composition, he knew the music he was playing.
That took some mentality. He knew every player he played behind.
Yes, he was a marvelous musician. Dave Tough was reading music as a boy scout, as a child. He was reading music at the age of 14.
Did he pick up at the piano at all, I don't remember.
Oh, no, he used to with one finger, had to be fun kind of like that. Lionel Hampton's.
Yes. But Dave also, in his own personality, I mean he blended with people personally on
Dave Tough was one of the most delightful you would ever want to meet, and had a brilliant sense of humor. I will never forget, Dave Tough was having an affair -- is this okay?

Having an affair with in those days, a corny bandleader's wife, who was sort of nympho-manic, and her husband -- the bandleader came in and found Dave and his wife together and Dave looked up at the man and said, 'Thank God, it's you.' And you know, when you think of this, this man was so --

Helen, I want to make a correction here. At that point, I said that Dave had been playing 50 years and that of course was a great mistake. What I mean to say was that he played, talking from this day and going back, he played that way 55 years ago. I have been playing 54 years and I think Dave played long before I, but he played really that same beat that same wonderful way, some 55 years ago.
So at that point, I think -- Dave died at the age of 48, so at that point, say, 1946, he had been playing then about 32 years. That would be right, he started at the age of 14 -- some 30-odd years.
